en.name: iBuddyPlay
en.subtitle: 22 two-player games, offline
en.short_description: 22 two-player games, on one phone or two. No account, no internet.
en.description:
BuddyPlay is 22 two-player games in one app. Pass one phone back and forth, or put two phones on the same Wi-Fi and play across them.

THE GAMES
Chess · Checkers · Reversi · Connect Four · Battleship · Ludo · Mancala · Nim · Mastermind · Tic-Tac-Toe · Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe · Dots and Boxes · Hangman · Word Duel · Trivia Battle · Twenty Questions · Pong · Air Hockey · Racer · Snake Battle · Tank Battle · Coin Flip & Dice.

TWO PHONES, NO SERVER
Host a match and your phone shows a pairing code. The other player joins over the same Wi-Fi network or your phone's hotspot — the two devices talk to each other directly over the local network. Nothing is relayed through a server, nothing needs an internet connection, and there is no account to create.

RIVALRIES
BuddyPlay remembers who you play and keeps the running score. Clear it whenever you like.

QUIET BY DESIGN
No ads. No sign-up. No analytics profile. Haptic feedback and a default game are the only settings you need to think about.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing BuddyPlay.

BuddyPlay is a collection of two-player games. There is no account, no sign-in, no purchase, no ads and no analytics, and nothing is relayed through a server. The app is locked to portrait because a board should not spin mid-move.

The one thing to plan for: two-device play needs two physical devices on the same Wi-Fi network or one phone's hotspot. A simulator cannot demonstrate it — there is no second device to discover. Everything in the app can still be reviewed on a single device, because every game is playable pass-and-play on one phone. Please use that path if you only have one device.

Also expected, so neither looks like a missing feature:
• Not every game supports two devices. Seventeen do — Royal Chess, Checkers, Reversi, Connect Four, Battleship, Dice Kingdom (Ludo), Mancala, Nim, Mastermind, Tic-Tac-Toe, Ultimate TTT, Dots & Boxes, Hangman, Word Duel, Trivia Battle, 20 Questions and Coin & Dice. The real-time ones — Pong, Air Hockey, Mini Racer, Snake Battle, Tank Battle — and the Pictionary Timer are single-device, and the app prints the reason on screen instead of greying a button out.
• Settings states outright that "Bluetooth pairing is not in this build". Bluetooth appears in the transport model but has no implementation, and the app says so rather than pretending otherwise.

Test instructions:
1. Launch the app. The home grid lists the games in three tiers with a filter above it. No sign-in, no onboarding, no permission prompt yet.
2. Tap any game, then "Play on this phone". Both players share the one phone; the full game runs with no network and no permission. This alone exercises every game in the app.
3. For two devices: on the first phone tap a game, then "Host for a nearby buddy". It shows a four-character pairing code (BUDD-xxxx) and its own address. iOS asks for local-network access at this point — the app uses UDP multicast discovery on port 47771 and then a direct TCP socket, declared as _buddyplay._tcp in Info.plist. Multicast discovery on iOS also needs the com.apple.developer.networking.multicast entitlement.
4. On the second phone, on the same network, tap "Join nearby game". The host appears in the scan list; check the pairing code matches before connecting.
5. If discovery finds nothing — which is what happens on a network with multicast blocked, or without the multicast entitlement — use "Join by address" on the same screen and type the address shown on the host phone (for example 192.168.1.20:54321). That path exists precisely for this case and connects without multicast.
6. Play a few moves and confirm they appear on both phones. Then open the Rivalries tab at the bottom to see the running score against that opponent, and clear it.
7. Open Settings for haptics, the default game, and the note about Bluetooth.

Privacy:
• Data collected: Nothing about you. No account, no profile, no sign-up. Rivalry scores, the device id behind the pairing code, and your settings are written to shared_preferences on the device.
• Network: Local only. The two phones talk directly to each other over the LAN or a hotspot. There is no server, no relay, and no internet connection is required at any point.
• Location, camera, microphone, contacts: None are requested. The only permission the app can trigger is local network access, and only when you host or join a two-device match.
• Tracking: None. Crash reporting is Firebase Crashlytics only, keyed on the transport and the default game — both non-personal. There is no advertising or analytics SDK, and the app does not read the advertising identifier, so no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
